messages:
incident-bot: Pager: latency SLO breach detected for streaming-api (p95 & p99). Rolling alert: 3m sustained p99 > 1200ms across eu-west2. Impact: streaming stalls reported by customers. Paging oncall.
oncall-priya: on it. confirming alert details now. link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/2463009876
Dmitri: seeing similar in grafana — big spike around 08:42 UTC, tail latency & retransmit spikes on flows to 10.2.0.0/16
Sarah: also getting customer slack thread — some sessions drop mid-stream. p95 at ~600ms but p99 jumps to 1.5s
Kevin: any change/deploys? I checked deploy bot: no rollout in last hour. @eng-infra FYI
eng-infra: no infra deploys. starting network checks.
Maria: triage checklist: 1) confirm region/az scope 2) NAT/egress errors 3) TLS handshake graphs 4) streaming proxy logs
oncall-priya: I'll run quick tcpdump on a couple of backends, Dmitri can you pull NAT metrics?
Dmitri: NAT gateway metrics: ephemeral port exhaustion trend upward, many TIME_WAIT ~ lots of short-lived TLS connections. here's a quick query: nat.ephemeral_in_use{region="eu-west2"} => 82% used (normally 20-30%)
Sarah: that could explain handshake retries and slow tail. do we have packetloss/drops? eng-infra?
eng-infra: checked interface counters on egress: tx errors small, but cross-AZ path shows increased retransmits and elevated RTT to outbound 3rd party IPs. suspect cross-zone routing asymmetry + NAT churn
oncall-priya: can you paste the tcpdump snippet?
Dmitri: tcpdump output (truncated):
```
08:42:11.123 IP backend1 > natgw: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
08:42:11.223 IP natgw > backend1: RST, seq 1, win 0
08:42:11.223 IP backend1 > natgw: Flags [S], seq 0, ack 0
08:42:11.423 IP natgw > backend1: Flags [S.], seq 1000, ack 1
```
Dmitri: lots of retries and occasional RSTs back from the NAT side. Also see many port remaps.
Kevin: any DNS issues? TLS handshake spikes sometimes from delayed A records
Maria: DNS latency looks normal for eu-west2 in last 30m, <20ms. Not primary suspect.
Sarah: customer impact — which customers? streaming endpoints are multi-tenant. SLO breach affects standard tier only? metrics show both free and paid interrupted but paid shows more because of higher concurrency
oncall-priya: immediate mitigation options: 1) expand NAT ephemeral port range or add extra NAT nodes 2) fail traffic to alternative egress AZ 3) increase connection reuse on proxies (short term config) 4) rolling restart of NAT nodes to clear bad state
eng-infra: we can spin up an additional NAT pool in eu-west2:action. provisioning takes ~3-4 mins to be routable
Dmitri: quick mitigation: add ephemeral port range on existing NAT proxies (iptables tweak) — risk minimal, do we have runbook? Maria?
Maria: runbook: NAT-ephemeral-exhaustion.md — steps: increase --hashlimit? actually we prefer add nodes. iptables changes risky under load.
oncall-priya: let's do parallel: provision extra NAT node + enable traffic steering to it. If that doesn't fall fast, consider short-lived iptables tweak on a single canary node.
eng-infra: creating natpool-aux-01 now. ETA 3m. I'll post when BGP/route announced.
Kevin: I'll open a temporary routing policy to shift 25% of egress to natpool-aux-01 once ready. Monitor p99.
(Small pause)
eng-infra: natpool-aux-01 provisioned and health checks pass. starting gradual shift: 10% -> 25% -> 50%
oncall-priya: shifting 10% now
Dmitri: after 10% shift: p99 dropped a bit from 1500ms -> 1100ms. retransmit rate down ~18% (short window)
Sarah: customers reporting partial improvement :thumbsup:
oncall-priya: shift to 25% now
Kevin: 25% complete. p99 trending 900ms and still falling. watching for new regressions
Maria: capturing logs for postmortem — saving a sample of streaming proxy logs and NAT stats
eng-infra: 50% shift done. p99 now ~420ms, p95 back to 120-180ms
Dmitri: good signal. ephemeral usage on legacy nat lowered from 82% -> 46%
oncall-priya: ok we have immediate relief. Next steps (short): keep natpool-aux active and finish shift to balanced egress. (mid): schedule NAT capacity bump and investigate root cause of port churn. (long): add connection pooling changes to streaming proxy to reduce short-lived TLS churn
Kevin: tagging this incident for SLA tracking and customer comms. @Maria can you draft initial customer note: what happened, impact, mitigation, ETA for full fix?
Maria: will draft and post to #customer-notices after we stabilize. getting timeline and severity
Sarah: action item: run flow logs to see whether specific external IPs caused retry storms (maybe rate-limited hosts or CDN misbehaving)
Dmitri: running flow logs now. also analyzing application behavior for aggressive reconnects from workers
oncall-priya: do we need to escalate to oncall lead? impact still high earlier but now improving. propose keep paging suppressed unless re-escalation
incident-bot: Incident annotated: 2463009876 - NAT egress port exhaustion + cross-zone retransmits -> added aux NAT pool and shifted traffic. Severity: P2 (under review). Logged at https://incidents.redwood.internal/2463009876
Maria: customer note draft ready (short): "We observed a transient networking issue in eu-west2 that caused increased handshake times and intermittent streaming stalls for some customers. We deployed an additional egress pool and shifted traffic; performance is restored for most users. Root cause investigation ongoing; we'll follow up with postmortem and timeline." Posting after final check.
Kevin: nice. plan to keep natpool-aux up for 6h and monitor. open a follow-up ticket for infra to increase baseline NAT capacity.
eng-infra: follow-up ticket: INFRA-3821 created. also enabling more granular metrics for ephemeral port allocation per subnet
oncall-priya: thanks team. I'll monitor for 30m, then hand back to SRE rotation. If p99 stays < 600ms we mark mitigated. Dmitri, Maria, please collect artifacts for postmortem.
Dmitri: saving tcpdumps, nat metrics, flow logs. will upload to incident ticket.
Sarah: adding customers impacted list and incident timeline to ticket.
oncall-priya: handing back to rotation. marking incident as mitigated at 08:58 UTC pending postmortem. :white_check_mark:
